reasons: The restating ("You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble") sits inside one BSB line, so no line says another again. Line 2, "Your breath is a fire that will consume you", carries the picture on in a different shape and is not a plain parallel line.

"He will go back the way he came" and "he will not enter this city" name two linked outcomes, but it is not plain that the second says the first again. Line 3 is the speech formula "declares the LORD". Not plain enough for an unsourced mark.

No line says another again. "What can I say?" is a question, "He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this" answers it, and "I will walk slowly all my years / because of the anguish of my soul" is one sentence over two lines.

"I had such great anguish; / but Your love has delivered me" tells of a turn from distress to rescue, not two parallel lines opposed in sense. "for You have cast all my sins behind Your back" gives a reason, not an opposite.

The address lines do say the same thing again: "O Zion, herald of good news" and "O Jerusalem, herald of good news." The commands do not. "Go up on a high mountain" and "Raise your voice loudly" are two different acts, climbing and then shouting, and the next line goes further still ("Lift it up"). So the second pair adds to the first instead of restating it. That is building or alternating lines, not plainly "same", and in doubt it fails.

"He tends His flock like a shepherd" is filled out by different acts ("gathers the lambs ... carries them ... gently leads the nursing ewes"), not said again. These are a run of description, not plainly paired lines.

In the BSB, line 2 gives the reason for line 1 ("you have not called on Me, O Jacob, / because you have grown weary of Me, O Israel"), so it is one sentence over two lines, not a restatement. The tags mark the conjunction "for" (H3588A), which carries no figure.

The lines are the craftsman's successive steps (measuring line, stylus, chisels, compass, fashioning). Each one adds a new act and none restates the one before. Calling a plain list of acts "building" would not show a figure plainly.
The verse is a narrative sequence: burns half, roasts meat, eats, warms himself and speaks. No line restates another.
The lines go step by step from making the god to bowing, praying and the words of the prayer. That is progression, not a restatement, and not a plain figure.

The four lines are a command, a reason, a creation claim and a promise. Line 3 repeats "you are My servant" but adds "I have made you", and the verse's shape (remember ... never forget) is not plainly "said twice". The tags fall on names and on "for", not on any figure.
Raising Cyrus, making his ways straight, rebuilding the city, freeing the exiles, then a qualifier and a speech formula: these are successive acts, and no line restates another.
The eight lines mix a speech formula, a run of creation verbs, a not/but pair and God's claim. No single relation holds across them, and no pair is plainly "said twice".

"unable to relieve the burden; / but they themselves go into captivity" does not set an opposite. It goes a step further in the same direction, and line 1 takes no part, so no live form is plain here.
The lines move from God's anger to handing the people over, then to Babylon's lack of mercy and the yoke on the elderly. Each line adds something and none restates the last.

"Listen to Me, O Jacob, / and Israel, whom I have called" is one address split over two lines. "I am the first, / and I am the last" pairs opposite ends and does not restate. No live form is plain at these words.
"I have not spoken in secret" and "from the time it happened, I was there" make different claims, and the verse then changes speaker. Nothing is said twice.

why: judge moved it to building, which no reader proposed
reasons: "I was bereaved and barren; / I was exiled and rejected" is a plain pair of lines on her desolation. But exile and rejection are new griefs, not other words for losing her children, so the second line adds to the first (building) rather than saying it again. The questions around the pair ("Who has begotten these for me?", "So who has reared them?") are not part of it.

"Rise up and sit on your throne" adds a picture nothing else restates. "O captive Daughter of Zion" only names the one addressed. "Shake off your dust!" and "Remove the chains from your neck" are different pictures, so no two lines plainly say the same thing.

"You are wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, 'There is no hope!'" is a concession inside one thought, and "You found renewal of your strength; therefore you did not grow weak" is cause and result. No line answers another with its opposite, and no other form is plain. The search keyed on "but".

"I have seen his ways, but I will heal him" is mercy despite sin, and the reader needs 57:17 to see that the ways were sinful. "I will guide him and restore comfort / to him and his mourners" goes on with the promise. These are not plain opposite lines.

No line restates the one before. "for He is the Maker of all things" gives a reason, and "Israel is the tribe of His inheritance" turns the relation around. The tags (Jacob, for, formed, all, he, Israel) carry no figure.
"for the LORD has spoken" gives a reason and does not restate "Listen and give heed. Do not be arrogant". The one tag, on "give ear", is a single word inside line 1, not a parallel line.

"Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her" is a plea that gets no answer. It is not a line set against its opposite, and the search only caught ", but". The tags spread over Zion, hands, commanded, Yahweh and Jacob, which carry no figure.
"I called out to my lovers, but they have betrayed me" tells of a call met with betrayal. It is not two lines opposed in sense, and lines 3-6 stand in no such relation.

"People have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me" is a lament with no reply, not an opposite line. The rest of the verse sets no opposite either. The place was caught on a mechanical ", but".

"cut off every horn of Israel", "withdrawn His right hand" and "burned in Jacob like a flaming fire" are three different acts. None restates another. The tags fall on names, verbs and prepositions and mark no figure.

The elders "sit on the ground in silence", throw dust and put on sackcloth, and "The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads". These are different mourning acts by different groups, not one line restated. The tags carry no figure.

"He left me without help" gives the outcome of "He forced me off my path and tore me to pieces" and does not restate it. Calling it "built on" would only describe two lines in a row, not a figure the words plainly show, so it does not go live.
"You have killed without pity" goes a step past "covered Yourself in anger and pursued us", so it adds rather than restates. It is not plain enough to go live under another form either.
"You said, 'Do not be afraid'" tells what God said after "You drew near when I called on You". It is a next step in the account, not a restatement and not a plain figure.

"The nursing infant's tongue / clings in thirst" (thirst) and "Little children beg for bread, / but no one gives them any" (hunger, with the new thought that no one gives) do not plainly say the same thing again. No two lines inside either sentence restate each other.

"Our fathers sinned and are no more, / but we bear their punishment" does set "fathers" against "we" with "but". Still, line 2 does not state the opposite of line 1. It completes it: "their punishment" cannot stand without line 1, and sin and its punishment are cause and effect, not opposites. "Building" fits at least as well, so the verse does not plainly show "opposite", and with that doubt the place fails.

"The rebels are deep in slaughter; / but I will chastise them all": the second line is God's answer to the sin, not its opposite. The search caught only the word "but". Calling it "built on" would be too loose to stand with no named writer behind it.
"They go with their flocks and herds / to seek the LORD, / but they do not find Him" is one sentence running over the lines: a search that fails, then its reason. No line is set against its opposite.
Lines 1-2 are one sentence. "They slash themselves for grain and new wine, / but turn away from Me" joins two charges and sets neither against an opposite. No form is plain at the marked words.

"Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, / and though they eat the meat, / the LORD does not accept them" is one sentence, and no BSB line restates another. The pairing of "remember their iniquity and punish their sins" sits inside a single line.

why: judge moved it to simile, which no reader proposed
reasons: No line sets the opposite of another, because "but will be to them like the bread of mourners" carries the thought on. The plain figure in the marked lines is the likeness with "like": their sacrifices will be "like the bread of mourners", which defiles all who eat it.

"Give them, O LORD— / what will You give?" breaks off and starts again and does not restate anything. "wombs that miscarry / and breasts that dry up" names two curses under one verb, and the second does not plainly say the first again. Too doubtful to go live.

"he struggled with the angel and prevailed; / he wept and sought His favor; / he found Him at Bethel / and spoke with Him there" tells events in order, each adding something new. Nothing is restated, and "built on" would be too loose to stand without a named writer.

"Labor pains come upon him, / but he is an unwise son" sets no line against its opposite. The birth picture is there, but which form and words carry it (metaphor, alternating lines) is not plain enough to go live with no named writer.

"their little ones will be dashed to pieces, / and their pregnant women ripped open" names two different groups of victims, so the second line adds to the first and does not restate it. Lines 1-2 are one running sentence. Calling it "said twice" is not plain from the verse.
"I will heal their apostasy; / I will freely love them, / for My anger has turned away from them" makes two different promises and then gives the reason. No line restates another.

"his splendor will be like the olive tree, / his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon" matches in form, but splendor and fragrance are different features, so the second line adds rather than restates. "His shoots will sprout" stands apart. "Said twice" is not plain.
Dwelling in his shade, growing grain and blossoming, and renown like the wine of Lebanon are three separate blessings. No line restates another.

"The grapevine is dried up, / and the fig tree is withered" names a different tree in each line, and the list grows to "all the trees of the orchard" and then to a new point, "the joy of mankind." Each line adds; none plainly restates the one before.

"They storm the city; / they run along the wall; / they climb into houses, / entering through windows like thieves" moves step by step from city to wall to houses to windows. Each line is a new stage, so no line restates another.

No line restates another. "who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain" adds to line 1, and "Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners" is a new promise. The lines only build, which is not a plain figure. One tag falls on H1961 "it will be", which carries nothing.

"but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph" completes the charge against their luxury. It is not a line set against its opposite in sense. Seeing drinking and anointing as the opposite of mourning goes beyond what the verse plainly shows, and the readers disagree, so it does not go live.

"as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink" is a comparison, and "They will drink and gulp it down; they will be as if they had never existed" moves on to the result. No line plainly restates another.

"For her wound is incurable" restates nothing. "it has reached even Judah; it has approached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem itself" goes a step further each time, and the readers disagree on whether it restates or builds. When in doubt it does not go live.

"they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them" is a refused answer, not a line opposite in sense. "He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done" continues it. The lines only build, and "hide His face" is already its own place.

"slow to anger / and great in power" adds rather than restates, and "will by no means / leave the guilty unpunished" is one clause split over two lines. The storm lines are at most a doubtful pair, since "clouds are the dust beneath His feet" adds a new picture. No plain restatement holds across the marked lines.

The tagged words, "the splendor of Jacob / like the splendor of Israel", are one clause making a comparison, not a line restating another. The BSB shows the same words, so "only in the original" is wrong. The pair the place would need is a different one from what its tags mark.

"GOD the Lord is my strength" stands over the next lines, and "He makes my feet like those of a deer; / He makes me walk upon the heights!" goes a step further rather than plainly restating. Whether it is "same" or "building" is not plain, so it does not go live.
"I will sweep away man and beast; / I will sweep away the birds of the air, / and the fish of the sea" adds new creatures to a list rather than restating, and the span also marks "declares the LORD".

"those who bow on the rooftops / to worship the host of heaven" and "those who bow down and swear by the LORD / but also swear by Milcom" are two different groups in the list carried on from 1:4. The second does not restate the first.

why: judge moved it to doubling, which no reader proposed
reasons: "O shameful nation" is only the people addressed and does not restate line 1, so "same" is wrong. The plain figure is the verb said twice for force in "Gather yourselves, gather together" (the Hebrew has the same verb, H7197B, twice), so it is kept as doubling on those words.

"These are the statutes and ordinances you must be careful to follow..." is one prose sentence with nothing going out and coming back in reverse order. The structure in the note belongs to the chapter, not this verse.

"I was glad when they said to me, / 'Let us go to the house of the LORD'" has no reversed order. The echo of "the house of the LORD" in 122:9 would be a frame, and these words mark only one end of it.
"Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good. / His loving devotion endures forever" has no reversed order. The opening "Give thanks" answered in 136:26 is a frame, and this marks only one end.
"O LORD, You have searched me / and known me" shows no reversed order. It is taken up in 139:23, "Search me, O God, and know my heart", in the same order, which would be a frame needing both verses.
"Hallelujah!" opening 149:1 and closing 149:9 is a frame, not a mirror, and this place marks all of 149:1 and nothing in 149:9.
"Hallelujah!" opening 150:1 and closing 150:6 is a frame, not a mirror, and this place marks all of 150:1 and nothing in 150:6.

The BSB sets 1 Corinthians 11:17 as one prose sentence: "In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good." Nothing in it comes back in reverse order. The search took its claim from Calvin's remark on 11:33, which is not in these words.

"And you were dead in your trespasses and sins," is one prose clause, with no lines that take turns. The past and present alternation is Bullinger's outline of the whole chapter and cannot be seen in this verse.
Colossians 2:8 is one prose sentence with no A B A' B' lines. The alternation is an outline of 2:8-23 brought in from outside the verse.

"Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our beloved fellow worker," is a plain letter greeting with nothing in reverse order. The eighteen-part introversion is Bullinger's outline of the whole letter, not something this verse shows.
